newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen firm on Nikkei losses, upside capped.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen firm on Nikkei losses, upside capped.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures edged higher in slow trade on Monday as Tokyo stocks continued to lose ground on worries about bad loan problems in Japan and the dollar's fall against the yen.
The dollar slid below 113 yen on news Japan's trade data for the first 20 days of June showed a surplus of 453.20 billion yen, almost double that of the same period a year ago.

The Nikkei share average was also hit by selling of construction and finance sector stocks following Friday's news that debt-laden Japanese construction firm Tokai Kogyo intended to apply for court protection from creditors.
The news eroded fears of an imminent rate hike in Japan, helping underpin Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures.
But dealers said the market showed limited upside.
The lead March Euroyen contract stood at 99.01 at 1115 GMT against an IMM close at 98.99 on volume of 3,525 lots.
September JGBs ended at 124.82 against a previous 125.13.

"March Euroyen should fall below 99.00 again. There's quite a lot of buying interest in the (September) Nikkei around 19,760. It's bounced back three times from those levels in recent months," a trader at a European futures house said.
The Nikkei 225 share index ended 262.83 points lower at 19,705.17 while SIMEX Nikkei futures for September lost 170 points to 19,760.

Eurodollar futures were little changed as participation was limited after a U.S. holiday last Friday and with no major U.S. economic data expected before the June Producer Price Index (PPI) at the end of the week.
"There was not much paper in the market today. It was mainly locals because it's going to be a quiet week before the PPI," the trader said.

He said the market looked strong technically but recent rises could have been overdone and 94.06 represented a good sell level for December Eurodollars. The contract ended at 94.055 against an IMM close at 94.045.
